title: Explorer: show readable keyword spellings on the title card
description:
## Summary

The explorer's title card shows keywords the way the store keeps them, stemmed, which reads as broken text. Show a readable spelling.

## Current behavior

The card for Iron Man (2008) lists its tags as "aggress", "middl east", "base on comic", "counterterror", "kidnap", "arm dealer", "altern dimens" and "pregnanc" on other titles. These are the stored, normalised and stemmed forms from the `keywords` namespace (`plex-db-ex-iyx.1`), not spellings a person would write.

## Desired behavior

Each tag on the card shows a readable spelling taken from `keyword_forms` (the table mapping every raw spelling to its stored form), for example the most common raw spelling of that stored keyword. The stored form stays the key everywhere a tag is clicked, searched or counted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The card for a title shows unstemmed tags; clicking one still selects the stored keyword.
- [ ] A stored keyword with no entry in `keyword_forms` falls back to its stored form.
- [ ] `docs/schema.md` is unchanged, since no table or column changes.
- [ ] `admin vet` green.

Saw this because: the title card built in `plex-db-ex-1u6.1`, viewed against the migrated store.
notes: Reuse readable_forms(conn) in plexdb/explore.py (added by 1u6.3): shortest raw spelling per stored keyword, ties by name; keyword_forms has no counts, so 'most common' is not available.

title: Explorer: titles-first map with zoom-level region labels
description:
## Parent

The "Explorer viewer" epic in this tracker.

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Rebuild the Map view as a titles-first scatterplot on the shared viewport, with tag labels over regions that refine as the view zooms in. Name the view "Title map".

## Current behavior

The map (`plexdb/explore.html`, `drawMap`, data from `/api/map`) draws every title as a point placed by UMAP over keyword vectors, with a hover tooltip and click-to-open. It has no zoom, no pan, no search and no region labels, and the page scrolls under the wheel.

## Desired behavior

- Uses the shared viewport, hover card, selection and search.
- **Region labels.** At full zoom-out, the most common tags in each dense region appear as large labels over that region. As the view zooms in, each region splits and finer tags appear, down to the individual title's tags in its card. The labels come from the same keyword data the map is built from.
- **Tag filter.** Selecting a tag (from a card or the search box) fades every title without it.
- **Title search** focuses the viewport on that title and its similar titles.
- The Movies/Shows toggle and the noise-tag exclusion keep working.
- The view is labelled "Title map" in the view switcher.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Full zoom-out shows at least 8 region labels; zooming into one region shows labels that were not visible before.
- [ ] Selecting a tag fades non-carriers; clearing restores.
- [ ] Movies and Shows both work, and a noise-marked tag stays out of the labels.
- [ ] Screenshots at three zoom levels, looked at.
- [ ] `admin vet` green.

## Blocked by

The shared viewport, hover card, selection and search item.
close_reason: Region labels on the title map landed in 1faa6da

title: Explorer: tags-first tag network of every tag above a threshold
description:
## Parent

The "Explorer viewer" epic in this tracker.

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Replace the Graph view with a tags-first network: every tag above a title-count threshold on screen at once, connected by co-occurrence, rendered on the shared viewport. Name the view "Tag network".

## Current behavior

`drawGraph` (`plexdb/explore.html:416`) draws the chosen tag plus its top 20 to 150 co-tags with Cytoscape and redraws around a new centre on every click. Only that neighbourhood is on screen. Nothing shows which titles carry a tag.

## Desired behavior

- **Whole network.** Nodes are tags carried by at least N titles. A "minimum titles per tag" slider sets N: default 25 (964 tags), range 3 (7,871 tags) to 100. An edge joins two tags that share titles, thicker for more shared titles; edges are capped per node so the picture stays readable. Node size is the title count.
- **Rendering.** Canvas, on the shared viewport item's component. Cytoscape is removed. The layout is computed once per threshold and cached; the implementer records where it runs (server or browser) and why.
- **Labels.** The largest tags are labelled at full zoom-out and smaller ones appear as the view zooms in.
- **Selecting a tag** highlights it and its neighbours, dims the rest, and opens a panel with the tag's title count, its strongest co-tags (each clickable), and the titles carrying it as a list with the title card's fields.
- **Search** by tag name focuses the node.
- The noise-marked tags the explorer already excludes stay excluded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At the default threshold the whole network is visible at once and pans and zooms at 30 frames per second or better, measured and reported.
- [ ] Moving the slider to 3 redraws without freezing the page for more than 2 seconds.
- [ ] Selecting a tag lists the titles carrying it.
- [ ] The view is labelled "Tag network" in the view switcher.
- [ ] Screenshots at threshold 25 and 3, looked at.
- [ ] `admin vet` green; `docs/file-map.md` updated if files moved.

## Blocked by

The shared viewport, hover card, selection and search item.

title: Explorer: shared pan/zoom viewport, hover card, selection and search
description:
## Parent

The "Explorer viewer" epic in this tracker.

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Add one 2D canvas viewport component that the tag graph and the title map both use: wheel zoom and drag pan that take over scrolling, a hover card, click-to-select with a clear button, and a search box.

## Current behavior

The wheel scrolls the page over both the Graph and Map views. The map (`explore.html`, `drawMap`) has a hover tooltip and click-to-open, no zoom, no pan, no search. The graph uses Cytoscape with its own separate interaction code. Nothing shows a poster, description or similar titles.

## Desired behavior

- **Viewport.** Over the canvas the wheel zooms toward the cursor and never scrolls the page. Drag pans. A reset control returns to the whole picture. Touch pinch and drag work at a narrow width.
- **Hit testing.** Hovering picks the nearest item in world coordinates through a spatial index, so a point that is 2 px wide at full zoom-out is hoverable once zoomed in.
- **Hover card** for a title: poster slot, title, year, studio, content rating, description slot, its tags, and its nearest similar titles taken from the `tmdb_similar` edges by rank. The poster and description slots show a placeholder until the poster source item is done; the card is complete without them.
- **Selection.** Click selects an item and pins its card. An X button on the card (and Esc) clears the selection.
- **Search box.** A title query focuses the viewport on that title and its similar titles. A tag query fades every item without that tag and leaves the rest at full strength. Clearing the box restores the view.
- **Endpoint.** One read-only `/api/title` call returns the card's fields for a given `item_id`. It follows the explorer's existing guards (size cap, concurrency cap, `application/json` on POST bodies).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scrolling the wheel over either canvas zooms it and the page's scroll position does not change.
- [ ] Dragging pans; a title pinned at 4x zoom is hoverable and shows its card with tags and similar titles.
- [ ] Clicking an item pins its card; the X button and Esc both clear it.
- [ ] Searching a title focuses it and its similar titles; searching a tag fades every non-carrier.
- [ ] Screenshots of hover, selection, title search and tag search, looked at.
- [ ] `admin vet` green.

## Out of scope

- Poster and description sources: see `plex-db-ex-oyg.2`.
- The tag graph's layout and the map's zoom labels (the two view items).
close_reason: Shared viewport, title card, search and full-screen shell landed on main (47d73a1)

title: Explorer viewer: tags-first network, titles-first map
description:
## Summary

Rebuild the tag explorer's Graph and Map views around what each one shows first. The graph shows tags first: every tag and how they connect. The map shows titles first: every title, placed by keyword similarity. Both use one shared viewport, hover card, selection and search, so they behave the same way.

## Why

Both views today fail the same way (`plexdb/explore.html`):

- The page scrolls under the mouse. The wheel scrolls the page instead of zooming the view, so small points are hard to hover.
- The graph (`drawGraph`, `explore.html:416`) draws only the chosen tag and its top 20–150 co-tags, then redraws from scratch when a node is clicked. The whole network is never on screen.
- Hovering or selecting a tag or title shows no titles, poster or description.
- There is no search, and a selection has no clear button.

Reference implementations checked against: the [Movie Map](https://mikeyguinness.com/movies/) (title scatterplot with hover, search, and tag labels that refine as you zoom) and [VOSviewer Online](https://app.vosviewer.com/) (whole-network term co-occurrence graph).

## Data sizes the design depends on

Measured on the pulled store: 12,721 movies, 1,643 shows, 20,419 distinct keywords. Keywords carried by at least 3, 10, 25 titles: 7,871, 2,507, 964.

## Done when

The three child items are closed and the Table view is unchanged.

title: plexdb-reader reads keywords across sources and resolves spellings
description:
## Parent

The "Taste Profile Spec" run epic in this tracker.

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Make the `plexdb-reader` crate read the source-agnostic `keywords` namespace and resolve keyword spellings through `keyword_forms`.

## Current behavior

The reader's bulk enrichment read and taste rollup take a namespace and return every row in it. Nothing reads `keyword_forms`, which the previous slice adds.

## Desired behavior

- Bulk enrichment and the taste-vector rollup return each `(key, value)` once per item, even when several sources carry it. The `source` column never reaches a caller.
- New read: a surface spelling → its stored keyword. The input is lowercased, trimmed and whitespace-collapsed, then looked up in `keyword_forms`. An unknown surface returns none, not an error.
- New read: a stored keyword → its surface spellings, for audit display.
- The crate's tests run against a fixture holding two sources.

## Key interfaces

- `enrichment_for_many` — same signature, results deduplicated across sources
- Taste rollup (`taste_vector_for`, pooled vector) — one weight per keyword, whatever its sources
- New surface → keyword read, returning an optional string
- New keyword → surfaces read, returning a list of strings

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A keyword two sources both carry appears once in `enrichment_for_many` for that item and counts once in the rollup.
- [ ] `Heists` resolves to the stored form of `heist`; `  Bank-Heist ` resolves the same as `bank heist`.
- [ ] An unknown surface returns none.
- [ ] Crate tests green.

## Out of scope

- Stemming in Rust. Only the Python writer stems.
- Refreshing etv-station's vendored copy (etv-station's own slice).

## Blocked by

- The "One `keywords` namespace with per-source rows" slice in this tracker.
acceptance_criteria: Keyword carried by two sources appears once in enrichment_for_many and the rollup; Heists resolves to stored heist; unknown surface returns none; crate tests green.
close_reason: plexdb-reader reads keywords across sources at schema v10, resolves spellings

title: One keywords namespace with per-source rows, normalized and stemmed
description:
## Parent

The "Taste Profile Spec" run epic in this tracker (its body holds the full spec; the etv-station half is tracked in etv-station's own beads).

## Category

enhancement

## Summary

Store keywords from every source in one `keywords` enrichment namespace, with the source recorded per row, values normalized and plural-stemmed, and a `keyword_forms` table mapping every raw spelling to its stored form.

## Current behavior

TMDB keywords are written as `(item_id, namespace='tmdb_keywords', key='keyword', value=<raw>)`. The source is encoded in the namespace name, values are stored as TMDB returned them, and a TMDB refresh deletes every row in the namespace. A second keyword source would need a second namespace, and any spelling variant would be a separate keyword.

## Desired behavior

- `enrichment` gains `source TEXT NOT NULL`, part of the primary key: `(item_id, namespace, source, key, value)`. Every write path supplies a source.
- TMDB keywords are written to `namespace='keywords', source='tmdb'`.
- One normalization function runs on every keyword before storage: lowercase, trim, collapse runs of whitespace, `-` and `_` become spaces, then Snowball English stemming word by word (`snowballstemmer`, approved as a new dependency).
- Every keyword write upserts `keyword_forms(surface TEXT PRIMARY KEY, keyword TEXT NOT NULL)` with the raw spelling and its stored form.
- A source's refresh deletes only rows `WHERE namespace='keywords' AND source=<that source>`. A keyword stays on an item while any source still lists it.
- A migration renames `tmdb_keywords` → `keywords`, backfills `source` (`tmdb` for keywords; a fitting source for other namespaces), re-normalizes and re-stems existing values, merging rows that now collide, and fills `keyword_forms` from the pre-migration values. Running it twice changes nothing.
- The existing health report adds keyword row counts per source and the `keyword_forms` row count, and fails if any `tmdb_keywords` row remains.
- ADR in `docs/adr/`: keywords are one source-agnostic namespace with a source column.

## Key interfaces

- `enrichment` table — new `source` column in the primary key
- `keyword_forms` table — new
- The keyword normalization function — one definition, used by every keyword writer and by the migration
- Health report — new keyword section and failure condition

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two sources both list `heist` for an item; one source's refresh drops it; the item still carries `heist`.
- [ ] `Heists`, `heist` and `bank-heist` / `bank heist` written by two sources collapse to single stored values, and every raw spelling appears in `keyword_forms`.
- [ ] The migration over a pre-migration fixture leaves no `tmdb_keywords` rows, every keyword row has `source='tmdb'`, and the health report passes.
- [ ] Running the migration a second time changes no rows.
- [ ] The existing test suite is green.

## Out of scope

- Adding a second keyword source.
- Grouping semantically similar keywords (plex-db-ex-sna).
- The Rust `plexdb-reader` crate (next slice).

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Two sources list heist, one retracts, heist survives; spelling variants collapse with every surface in keyword_forms; migration over pre-migration fixture passes health check; second migration run changes nothing; suite green.
close_reason: Landed on main at 8b11143: one keywords namespace with per-source rows, normalization and Snowball stemming, keyword_forms, schema v10 migration, source-scoped refresh, cursor, migration guard and fs-repair merges.

title: Taste Profile Spec
description:
# Taste Profile Spec

## Problem Statement
A taste-cosine pool can't be steered except by dropping a keyword (`exclude_keywords`) or tilting it toward one CEL-defined set (`influence`, positive only). A channel author can't say "more heist, less horror, more Michael Mann, less like *Grown Ups*", can't build a pool around a hand-picked list of films without the account's watch history mixed in, and can't reason about a weight's size, because the watch-history taste vector is on a play-count scale about 20× any hand-authored number. Underneath that, keywords are stored under a source-named namespace (`tmdb_keywords`) with no normalization. A second keyword source would create a second namespace to query, and spelling variants of one keyword would count as different keywords.

## Solution
A pool gets a **taste profile**: a list of signed weights on keywords, on any catalog tag namespace, on individual items and on CEL-defined sets. These are written inline on the pool and/or loaded from shared profile files. The scorer adds up each keyword's weight across entries and routes the net positive keywords to a favor term (added on top of the fraction) and the net negative ones to a disfavor term (added on the bottom), so a score never goes negative. The watch-history vector is normalized so its strongest keyword is 1.0, and `taste_weight` scales it. At 0 the pool ranks on the profile alone. The profile replaces `influence`. In plex-db-ex, keywords from every source live in one `keywords` namespace, normalized and plural-stemmed at write time. Each row records its source, so a source refresh removes only the keywords that source retracted. A `keyword_forms` table maps every raw spelling ever seen to its stored form, so etv-station matches profile entries without doing any stemming itself.

## User Stories
1. As a channel author, I want to give a keyword a positive weight, so that films carrying it rank higher on that pool.
2. As a channel author, I want to give a keyword a negative weight, so that films carrying it rank lower without being excluded.
3. As a channel author, I want to weight a genre, director, cast member, writer, producer, country, label, studio or content rating, so that I can steer on metadata that isn't a TMDB keyword.
4. As a channel author, I want to weight an item by external id (`imdb:tt…`, `tmdb:…`, `tvdb:…`), so that "more like this film" or "less like this film" holds up across renames and rescans.
5. As a channel author, I want to weight an item by `"Title (Year)"`, so that I can write a profile from memory when the title is unambiguous.
6. As a channel author, I want an ambiguous or unmatched title, or an unmatched id, to fail the generation and list what it found, so that a typo never quietly weights nothing.
7. As a channel author, I want to weight a CEL-defined set (such as a collection) positively or negatively, so that a curated list can pull a pool toward itself or push it away.
8. As a channel author, I want an item or set entry to spread its weight over its members' keywords and genres by share of members, so that a 20-film set and a 200-film set at the same weight mean the same thing.
9. As a channel author, I want entries that disagree on one keyword to net out, so that "+2 heist" plus "−1 *Heat*" leaves heist favored by 1.
10. As a channel author, I want `taste_weight: 0` to rank a pool on the profile alone, so that I can build a pool around a seed list with no watch history involved.
11. As a channel author, I want the watch-history term normalized so its top keyword is 1.0, so that a hand weight of 1 means "as strong as my strongest taste" on every account.
12. As a channel author, I want to keep a person's standing likes and dislikes in one shared profile file that several pools include, with each pool's own entries added after it, so that I don't copy the same dislikes into every pool.
13. As a channel author, I want a profile keyword written in any spelling the library has seen (`Heists`, `bank-heist`) to match the stored keyword, and one that matches nothing to fail the channel load, so that spelling never silently breaks a weight.
14. As a channel author, I want `admin audit` to show each pick's favor and disfavor scores, which profile entries contributed, the file each came from and the keywords' original spellings, so that I can tune weights against real numbers.
15. As the plex-db-ex operator, I want every keyword source written into one `keywords` namespace with its source recorded, so that queries name one namespace no matter how many sources feed it.
16. As the plex-db-ex operator, I want a TMDB refresh to remove only keywords TMDB retracted, and to keep one another source still lists, so that sources never delete each other's data.
17. As the plex-db-ex operator, I want keywords lowercased, trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, `-`/`_` turned into spaces and plural-stemmed before storage, so that spelling variants from any source merge into one keyword.
18. As the operator of channels 002 and 003, I want their `influence` sets carried over as `set:` entries and re-tuned, so that they keep their tilt after `influence` is removed.

## Implementation Decisions

**plex-db-ex: enrichment schema (migration).**
```diff
 enrichment (
     item_id, namespace,            -- 'tmdb_keywords' → 'keywords'
+    source TEXT NOT NULL,          -- existing rows: 'tmdb'
     key, value,                    -- value: normalized + stemmed
     fetched_at,
-    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, namespace, key, value)
+    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, namespace, source, key, value)
 )
+keyword_forms (surface TEXT PRIMARY KEY, keyword TEXT NOT NULL)
```
- Every write path that inserts enrichment rows supplies a `source`. A source's refresh deletes only rows `WHERE namespace = ? AND source = ?`.
- The migration renames the namespace, backfills `source = 'tmdb'`, re-normalizes and re-stems existing keyword values (merging any rows that now collide) and fills `keyword_forms` from the pre-migration values. Other namespaces (`tmdb_edges` cursors and the like) get a source too, but their meaning doesn't change.
- Normalization is one function: lowercase, trim, collapse runs of whitespace, `-` and `_` become spaces, then English Snowball stemming, word by word. plex-db-ex is the only place this rule runs.
- plex-db-ex's existing health report adds keyword row counts per source, the `keyword_forms` row count, and a failure if any `tmdb_keywords` rows remain. That's the check that the migration ran on a given datastore, the prod one included.
- New dependency: `snowballstemmer` (PyPI, Snowball project, 3.1.1 released 2026-06-03). It needs the user's approval before it's added.

**plexdb-reader (plex-db-ex crate, vendored into etv-station).**
- Keyword reads (`enrichment_for_many`, the taste rollup) take the `keywords` namespace and return each distinct `(key, value)` once per item across sources.
- New read: resolve a surface spelling to its stored keyword through `keyword_forms`, after the same lowercase/trim/whitespace step. Returns nothing for an unknown surface.
- A read that returns the surface spellings for a stored keyword, for audit display.
- etv-station's vendored copy is refreshed with the pin hash updated in the same commit.

**etv-station: the profile is a pool field, not opaque `config`.** `profile` and `profile_files` sit beside `sources` on a plugin pool, because the station has to parse them, resolve them and fail the load on bad entries. That can't happen inside `config`, which the station treats as opaque. `taste_weight` stays in `config`, since it's a scoring tunable the script owns.
```yaml
- name: movies
  plugin: "../plugins/taste-cosine.rhai"
  profile_files: ["../profiles/pierce.yaml"]      # entries loaded first, in list order
  profile:
    - { keyword: heist,              weight:  2.0 }
    - { genre: Horror,               weight: -1.0 }
    - { director: Michael Mann,      weight:  1.0 }
    - { item: "imdb:tt0113277",      weight: -1.0 }
    - { item: "Grown Ups (2010)",    weight: -1.0 }
    - { set: 'item.collections.contains("…")', weight: 3.0 }
  config: { taste_weight: 1.0 }
```
- An entry has exactly one reference key: `keyword`, a catalog namespace name (`genre`, `label`, `cast`, `director`, `writer`, `producer`, `country`, `studio`, `content_rating`), `item`, or `set`. It also has a required finite, non-zero `weight`. Anything else is refused at load, naming the file and entry.
- **The station resolves references. The script does all weight math.** This follows ADR 0002: the station supplies inputs and never computes a score.
  - `keyword` → the stored keyword via `keyword_forms`. Unknown → the load fails.
  - `item` → one `entry_id`, by external id through the catalog's external-id table, or by exact title plus year. Zero or several matches → the generation fails, listing the matches.
  - `set` → member `entry_id`s via the same CEL resolution `sources` uses.
  - Catalog tag namespaces → matched by lowercase equality against catalog tags. No stemming.
- The script receives `ctx.profile`: an ordered list of resolved entries. Each carries its kind, namespace and value (for keyword and tag entries) or member items (for item and set entries), its weight, and its origin (a file path or `inline`).

**etv-station: `taste-cosine.rhai` scoring.**
```text
build profile maps
  for each entry in ctx.profile
    keyword / tag entry → add weight to (namespace, value)
    item / set entry    → for each (namespace, value) over members' keywords + genres:
                            add weight × (members carrying it / member count)
  net > 0 → favor map; net < 0 → |net| into disfavor map; 0 → dropped
score candidate
  taste    = cosine(candidate keywords, taste vector ÷ its max weight)
  favor    = Σ over namespaces of cosine(candidate's values in ns, favor map in ns)
  disfavor = same over the disfavor map
  score    = (taste_weight·taste + favor) / (1 + unusual_weight·house + disfavor)
  idf and the sqrt(count) divisor are computed per namespace
```
- `influence`, `influence_weight` and `enrichment_namespace() = "tmdb_keywords"` are deleted. The script reads the `keywords` namespace.
- `taste_weight` defaults to 1.0. At 0 the taste vector isn't fetched.
- Audit detail per pick adds `taste_weight`, `favor_score`, `disfavor_score`, and the contributing entries with origin and surface spelling. `influence_*` fields go away.

**etv-station: reading a profile back without a generation.** The `taste-debug` binary prints, for each profile-bearing pool, the resolved profile: every entry with its origin, what it resolved to (stored keyword, `entry_id`, member count), and the net favor and disfavor maps per namespace after netting. `taste-debug --resolve <surface>` prints the stored keyword a spelling resolves to, or says it's unknown. That's how an agent checks a profile edit before deploying it.

**Deploy config.** 002-for-pierce and 003-for-madi replace `influence` + `influence_weight` with a `set:` entry, re-swept with `tools/taste-debug.sh` under the normalized taste scale. `deploy/appdata/` is gitignored, so this is a hand edit in the primary checkout, not an agent slice.

## Testing Decisions
- Test through the public seams that already exist, at behavior level:
  - **plex-db-ex**: the enrichment write/refresh path and the schema migration, with store-level tests. Two sources listing one keyword, one retracts, the keyword survives. Spelling variants from two sources collapse to one row. The migration on a pre-migration fixture yields the `keywords` namespace, a `tmdb` source and a filled `keyword_forms`. Prior art: `tests/test_enrich_tmdb.py`, `tests/test_schema.py`.
  - **plexdb-reader**: distinct keywords across sources, and surface lookup, in the crate's own tests.
  - **etv-station config load**: bad entries, unknown keyword, ambiguous title and unmatched id each fail naming the entry. `profile_files` order. Prior art: the `sources:` load-refusal tests.
  - **etv-station scorer**: direct `pick()` against a hand-built datastore and catalog fixture, the style of `crates/etv-station/tests/taste_cosine_scorer.rs`. Hand-computed favor and disfavor scores for a named title. Netting (+2 keyword, −1 item sharing it → +1). `taste_weight: 0` ranks on the profile alone. A negative-only profile never produces a negative score. A 20-member and a 200-member set with the same keyword shares score identically. `influence` is gone.
- The vendored-reader pin test (`vendor_plexdb_reader_pin.rs`) must pass with the refreshed hash.
- Final check: `admin audit` on 002 shows the new fields against the live datastore after the deploy edit.

## Out of Scope
- Grouping semantically similar keywords (`heist` / `bank robbery`) by embedding similarity — plex-db-ex-sna.
- A TMDB recommendation/similar-title term for item entries — etv-station-yl8w.
- Stemming catalog tag namespaces (genres, cast, …). They're matched by lowercase equality only.
- Adding a second keyword source. This spec only makes the schema ready for one.
- Profiles on scorer plugins other than `taste-cosine.rhai`.

## Further Notes
- Order across repos: plex-db-ex schema + normalization + `keyword_forms` → plexdb-reader changes → vendored refresh in etv-station → station profile resolution → scorer → deploy config edit. The datastore migration must run on the prod datastore before an etv-station build reading `keywords` deploys. An old station against a migrated store (or the reverse) finds no keywords.
- On a `unit: show` pool, the scorer ranks shows, but `ctx.sets` items are episodes. Genre and other tag matching for show pools needs the show's own tags. Whether episodes carry the show's genres in the catalog is unverified.
- `exclude_keywords` values go through the same `keyword_forms` resolution as profile keywords.
- Glossary terms for etv-station's `docs/CONTEXT.md` (proposed as slate rows, written on `go`): **Taste profile** (a pool's signed weights over keywords, tags, items and sets), **Profile entry** (one reference plus one weight), **Favor / disfavor** (the net-positive and net-negative halves of a taste profile).
- Candidate ADRs: "keywords are one source-agnostic namespace with a source column" (plex-db-ex), and "the taste profile replaces the influence set; the station resolves, the script weighs" (etv-station).

title: Query tab: bound memory for a large sort or recursive CTE inside the 5 s window
description: SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH stops a single oversize value, but a statement such as WITH RECURSIVE ... SELECT x FROM c ORDER BY x builds rows until the 5 s timer fires, inside the plexdb schedule process that also runs the sweep. Not measured: run it against the real store and record peak memory first. Then decide on a per-statement row or byte budget (for example counting rows in the progress handler is not possible, so consider a cursor-side limit or running the query in a subprocess with a memory rlimit).

title: Architecture: the explorer writes its saved queries into a consumer's directory
description: In the container the login-less explorer writes explore-queries.json next to the published snapshot, which is the etv-station's own /snapshot data directory. Anyone who can reach the explorer port can add or delete saved queries, with no limit on how many (up to 1 MB each, MAX_BODY). plexdb/explore.py make_server: saved_path or store_path.with_name(SAVED_FILE). Options: a dedicated rw bind mount for the file (saved_path passed from serve_in_background), or plex-db-ex-bsh (the explorer in its own container with a snapshot-only mount), which removes the shared directory. Either way cap the entry count and total size.

title: Poster view for titles in the explorer
description:
A poster view for the tag explorer: show a title's poster next to its title, for movies and shows, wherever the explorer lists titles (the Tags tab's title list, the Query tab's results once oyg.1 labels ids).

## What is unsettled

The store holds no image and no image location. Where a poster comes from is the decision this item has to make first:

1. **Plex thumb.** `plex_items.rating_key` gives the Plex item, and Plex serves `/library/metadata/<rating_key>/thumb`, but only with `PLEX_TOKEN`. The explorer runs with no login on the host, so serving that image means proxying it through the explorer, which lets anyone who reaches the port spend the token. Needs the token kept server-side, a length and rate limit, and a decision on whether the deployed container may talk to Plex at all (ADR-0004: Plex is the required source, so it may).
2. **TMDB poster path.** TMDB's image CDN is public, needs no token, and a `poster_path` is one string per title. It would be a new enrichment fact (namespaced, `enrichment_cursor` for the fetch, `fetched_at` per CLAUDE.md) written by the existing TMDB sweep, and `docs/schema.md` changes with it. Costs a store change and a re-sweep across the library, rate-limited.
3. **Neither in the store: the browser fetches from Plex or TMDB directly.** The explorer sends only ids. Costs a Plex URL and token in the page, which the login-less explorer must not carry.

## Scope once that is decided

- Poster beside the label in the Query tab results and in the Tags tab title list; a placeholder tile when a title has none.
- Lazy loading, fixed aspect ratio so the table does not jump.
- Works at a narrow width.

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded in `docs/adr/` (image source, and where any token lives).
- A screenshot of the Query tab showing posters, looked at.
- No secret in any committed file; `docs/schema.md` updated if a fact is added.

title: SQL query tab with guards, saved queries and recipes
description:
Add a "Query" tab to the read-only tag explorer (`plexdb/explore.py`, `plexdb/explore.html`). The user pastes SQL, runs it against the store, sees rows, and saves named queries. Purpose: prototype etv-station "taste queries" (Rhai scripts reading this store through six reader accessors) by learning the schema hands-on. No dependency on etv-station: no imports, no shelling out, stdlib only, no new packages.

## Decided design

1. Raw SQL tab. Saved queries live in a JSON file outside the store (ADR-0001: the store is single-writer; the explorer never writes `plexdb.db`).
2. No query builder in this item. A later item adds a form that generates SQL into the editor.
3. Guards on the SQL box, active everywhere the explorer runs (local and the deployed container, which has no login):
   - fresh read-only connection per request, reusing the `mode=ro` opener in `plexdb/store.py` (near line 102)
   - `PRAGMA query_only=ON`
   - `Connection.set_authorizer` allowing only SQLITE_SELECT, SQLITE_READ, SQLITE_FUNCTION, SQLITE_RECURSIVE; deny everything else (ATTACH, PRAGMA, writes, DDL)
   - `set_progress_handler` aborting after 5 seconds
   - row cap 500 via `fetchmany`; response carries `truncated: true` when more existed
   - one statement only

## Backend (`plexdb/explore.py`, extend the existing ThreadingHTTPServer handler; it has only `do_GET` today)

- `POST /api/query` body `{"sql": "..."}` returns `{"columns": [...], "rows": [[...]], "row_count": n, "truncated": bool, "elapsed_ms": n}`. SQL error or authorizer denial returns HTTP 400 `{"error": "<sqlite message>"}`. BLOB values render as `<blob N bytes>`.
- `GET /api/saved` lists `{"name","sql","note"}`; `PUT /api/saved` upserts by name; `DELETE /api/saved?name=...`. Storage is one JSON file (e.g. `explore-queries.json`), written atomically (temp file + rename). Cap the request body size.
- The file must persist in the deployed container. Find where the explorer reads the store there (`plexdb/schedule.py`, `admin.toml` `[docker_run]`, `docs/development.md`) and which directory is a writable persistent mount. If none exists without changing deploy config, keep the file beside the store and state in the report what the deploy change would be. Never write a host path, hostname or secret into a committed file.
- Recipes: a fixed list of read-only queries, the SQL equivalent of the etv-station reader accessors. Read (do not import) `/Users/pierce/Projects/etv-station/vendor/plexdb-reader/src/lib.rs` for the accessors and their SQL, and `/Users/pierce/Projects/etv-station/examples/plugins/taste-cosine.rhai` for how they are used (`enrichment_for`, `enrichment_for_many`, edges, `watched_units`, `watched_units_for`, `taste_vector_for`, `pooled_taste_vector`). Copy the SQL text into this repo with editable placeholders. Add 3 or 4 orientation recipes (row counts per table, top enrichment keys per namespace, plays per account). Every recipe must run against the real schema.

## Frontend (`plexdb/explore.html`)

Match the existing tabs' look and code style. Query tab: SQL textarea (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter runs), Run button, result table (sticky header, scrollable), status line (row count, elapsed ms, truncated notice, errors in red), saved-queries list (click loads into the editor; save with name and optional note; delete), recipes list (click loads into the editor). Works at a narrow width.

## Tests

One focused test per behavior, sized like neighbouring tests: authorizer rejects a write, ATTACH and PRAGMA; row cap sets `truncated`; saved-query round trip including delete; a runaway recursive CTE hits the timeout.

## Docs

`docs/file-map.md` if files are added; the explorer's docs page and `docs/roadmap.md` only where they describe the explorer. No schema change, so `docs/schema.md` is untouched. Add this feature's verification path to `.claude/skills/verify-project`.

## Acceptance

- `admin vet` is green.
- Run the explorer locally on its own port, drive the Query tab in a browser, screenshot a real result and a rejected `DELETE`, and look at both images. Report their absolute paths.
- Stop the explorer server before returning.

title: Architecture: /api/title has no concurrency cap
description:
## Summary

Put a concurrency cap on `/api/title`, the way `/api/query` has one.

## Current behavior

`/api/title` in `plexdb/explore.py` runs two indexed reads per request with no limit on how many run at once. Only `/api/query` has a concurrency cap. The explorer has no login and listens on a host port.

## Desired behavior

`/api/title` and the other GET routes that read the store share the explorer's existing cap, or each has its own, and a request over the cap gets a 429 with a short body.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test opens more concurrent `/api/title` requests than the cap and sees a 429 for the excess.
- [ ] `admin vet` green.

Saw this because: the code review of `plex-db-ex-1u6.1` noted it; the endpoint was added there.

title: Explorer: measure the pinned card's space instead of hard-coding it
description:
## Summary

Measure the space the pinned title card and the tag panel occupy instead of hard-coding it, so the focus box stays clear of them at every window size.

## Current behavior

The area kept clear of the pinned card is fixed in `plexdb/explore.html`: a right column 340px wide plus 40px, and the bottom half on a narrow window. On a very short narrow window the free height can reach zero. At 600px wide or less the count and hint line is hidden while a card or the tag panel is open, because both dock at the bottom.

## Desired behavior

The clear rectangle comes from the panels' measured bounding boxes. The count and hint line stays reachable at every width, for example by moving to the top of the viewport when the bottom is occupied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At 1300x850 and 400x800, a title search leaves every focused point outside the card, computed from the measured boxes.
- [ ] At 400x400 the free height is above zero or the card collapses to its title row.
- [ ] The count line is visible at 400px wide with a card open.
- [ ] Screenshots at the three sizes, looked at.

Saw this because: the blind review of `plex-db-ex-1u6.1` scored it 30 and 25.

title: Explorer: one helper for fitting a set of points into the viewport
description:
## Summary

In `plexdb/explore.html`, `viewFor` and `focusOn` each normalise the padding and derive the view centring themselves, and the bounding-box loop appears twice (`syncMapItems`, `focusOn`). Extract one helper for fit-a-set-of-points-into-the-viewport.

## Current behavior

Two functions compute the same fit. A change to padding or centring has to be made in both.

## Desired behavior

One helper takes a set of points and the free rectangle and returns the view. `viewFor`, `focusOn` and the bounding-box loops call it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One implementation of the fit; the other call sites use it.
- [ ] Reset, title search focus and tag search focus behave as before, checked in the browser.
- [ ] `admin vet` green.

Saw this because: the blind review of `plex-db-ex-1u6.1` scored it 35.

title: Title map: pin the percentile clip with a test, compare the shows map by eye, build the amd64 image
description: No test pins the 1st-99th percentile clip (border landing, 0..1 range) in title_map; needs a small-store fixture. The shows map (1,547 points) was redrawn under the tuned UMAP settings but never compared visually with t-SNE. docker build --platform linux/amd64 has not run with umap-learn, numba and llvmlite added; run it before admin deploy.

title: Explorer map: keep the default map on screen when the live noise draw fails, and never show a blank canvas on a stale stored map
description: plexdb/explore.html:257-262: if the live noise request fails after the default map has shown, the catch sets map.data and map.key to null and the canvas goes blank. On first load with a stale stored map the canvas is also blank until the live draw lands. Fixing either changes UI, so verify with a screenshot.

title: Widen the title-map fingerprint so a same-size rewrite cannot serve a stale map
description: keyword_fingerprint (plexdb/explore.py:368-385) covers keyword row count, title count and max fetched_at. A wipe and rewrite of the same size with older timestamps, or an items row whose type flips, leaves title_map_state matching and a stale map served as fresh. The test covers additions only. Found by the wrap-up review of feat/y1l-precompute-title-map.

title: Group semantically similar keywords by embedding similarity
description:
Different keywords with the same meaning (heist / bank robbery / robbery) are stored as separate facts, so the etv-station taste scorer counts one taste two or three times. This happens with TMDB alone today, and more once a second keyword source lands in the shared `keywords` namespace.

Consider grouping them automatically by embedding similarity, so similar keywords resolve to one canonical keyword before scoring.

Out of scope until then: spelling and format variants (case, whitespace, hyphens), which the `keywords` namespace work normalizes at write time.

Open questions: which embedding model (a new dependency), similarity threshold, whether merges are reviewed before they apply, and whether grouping happens at write time or read time.
